chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Uthman ibn Ziyad, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a debt upon a man, and he intends to sell his house so that he may pay me.' He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I seek refuge for you with Allah that you should take him out from the shade of his head.'

key_terms.ظِلُّ الرَّأْسِ: shade of the head (metaphor for one's home or place of residence)
key_terms.يَقْضِيَنِي: he pays me / settles the debt

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on forcing a debtor to sell their house to pay off a debt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises the creditor to accept payment from the debtor's general assets rather than forcing the sale of his home, preserving the debtor's dignity and shelter. This ruling highlights the Shia legal principle of 'Zill al-Ras' (the shadow of the head), emphasizing that a person's primary residence is protected from forced liquidation to ensure basic human comfort and social stability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Usman Bin Ziyad who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There is a debt for me upon a man and he intends to sell his house, so he can pay me’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge for you with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that you should take him out from the shade of his head’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Flamid from ‘Uthman ibn Ziyad who has said the following: “

Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a man owes me a certain amount and wants to sell his house to pay me. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I seek protection for you with Allah against taking him out of the shadow on his head.’”
